BOTH arms. The dense coalescedReduction (algo.cuh:243-254) is `weighted_vertex_deg_dense_kernel` and accumulateWeights over the CSR (algo.cuh:62-91) is `weighted_vertex_deg_csr_kernel`; `need_ja_compute` (runner.cuh:257) is implemented so loop 1 fills `ja` on every weighted RBC batch (DEVIATION 29). Both of their reducers close on a lane-width-shaped CUB stage and are REPLACED by `pinned_block_sum` at the matrix's K_LIB_WEIGHTED_VERTEX_DEG width (DEVIATION 28). Their `if (weight_sum > 0)` guard at :90 is deliberately not copied; ours writes every row. Reaches the public API as DBSCAN(sample_weight=). GATED 2026-09-01 ON APPLE, and UNGATED from the day it landed until that morning: all four weighted checks were written and NONE had ever compiled -- `DeadArgumentElimination surveyUse failed`, an LLVM pass assertion, took the whole dbscan build down. The cure is the OPTIMIZATION LEVEL, not the source: `check-dbscan` builds at -O1, where -O3 and -O2 both assert and -O1 and -O0 both build, DeadArgumentElimination being an -O2-and-above pass. Four candidate source rewrites were tried first and all four still asserted at -O3. `pixi run check-dbscan` now prints all seven OK lines. A THREE-VENDOR LEG IS OWED; nothing weighted has run on an H100 or an MI325X

DBSCAN(metric='cosine', algorithm='brute'). Their in-place row normalization (rowNorm + matrixVectorOp on the device) is HOST code here, core/cosine_rows.mojo, compiled into both bindings (ascending pinned fold, identical_sqrt, identical_div), so the unit rows carry the same bits on every column; the L2 kernel then runs against Float32(2 * eps) (dbscan_metric_threshold). A zero-norm row is refused by name (theirs divides by zero). DBSCAN.predict takes the same path (core/labeled_reference_*predict.mojo scale refs and queries). The ball cover (algorithm='rbc') is refused for cosine by name: its radii and bounds compare against the radius, not 2 * eps. Lane x-cluster-dbscan-metrics

column3: The L1 eps neighborhood (DEVIATION 27) is BRUTE FORCE only. `neighbors/impl/ball_cover/common.mojo::eps_dist_sq` and the three landmark bounds at registers.mojo:280,:422,:547 compute Euclidean distance, so the index cannot answer an L1 query. NOT a property of the algorithm: ball-cover pruning rests on the triangle inequality, which L1 satisfies. Owed to the neighbors lane; until then DBSCAN(metric='manhattan') refuses algorithm='rbc' by name and names 'brute'

DBSCAN(metric='precomputed'): x is the n x n distance matrix, eps_precomputed_neigh_kernel (dbscan/impl/neighbors/epsilon_neighborhood.mojo) writes adj = D <= Float32(eps) and vd by an integer block sum per row, the host oracle reads the same row. No search, so `algorithm` does not apply (scikit-learn ignores it too). A non-square or negative matrix is refused by name; prediction_data=True is refused (predict needs query distances to the core samples). Lane x-cluster-dbscan-metrics
